summary.text: A male with coronary artery disease, dyslipidemia and a remote smoking history had a 6.7 cm juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm repaired by open aortobiiliac repair with a Dacron graft in 2022, with an uneventful recovery. Two years after the procedure he presented to the emergency department with acute abdominal pain and bilateral limb ischemia, Rutherford class IIa, with pain, paresthesia and initial lower extremity weakness and discoordination.

Urgent CTA showed complete thrombosis of the aortobiiliac graft. After therapeutic systemic intravenous heparin his motor strength and coordination returned, and endovascular rescue was attempted with bilateral percutaneous transfemoral thrombolysis using a 2 mg TPA bolus through each perfusion catheter then a 0.5 mg/hr infusion for 24 hours. Angiography after 24 hours showed a patent graft, but repeat CTA still showed a significant thrombus burden.

Noting that no obvious cause of graft thrombosis was apparent, a decision was made to re-line the graft using the CERAB technique. Via percutaneous bilateral common femoral access, a 22 mm × 37 mm Bentley Aortic Begraft was deployed in the proximal graft, a neo-aortic bifurcation was created with 8 mm × 79 mm Gore VBX stents, and the limbs were extended with Bentley Begraft Peripheral stent grafts. Completion angiography confirmed successful re-lining.

The postoperative course was uneventful and he was discharged home on 81 mg of aspirin and therapeutic anticoagulation with apixaban; the COMPASS protocol was not selected due to financial constraints. Follow-up CTA at 2 months showed a widely patent graft with no evidence of residual thrombus, and duplex at 6 and 12 months confirmed ongoing patency, absence of restenosis and a stable ankle-brachial index.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status not_inspected in annotation figures; actual JPEGs inspected in the separate visual submission.
Age 67 is attached to both the initial aneurysm presentation and the presentation two years later; both age items are review-only and the age is kept out of the label and summary.
Abstract states limb ischemia without motor impairment while the case text reports initial lower extremity weakness and discoordination; abstract item kept review-only.
Discussion states absence of significant comorbidity and an otherwise healthy patient alongside documented coronary artery disease and dyslipidemia; kept review-only.
Duplex at "6 and 12 months" is one source statement; recorded as one item per finding with the literal time text "6 and 12 months"; duplex images "not shown".
Several discussion sentences about the patient are authors' reasoning (options considered, judgments); recorded as considered/possible, not as performed.
Generic literature, background and interpretive claims (e.g. mortality and patency rates from cited studies, claims about the technique) are not patient facts.

Several patient-specific statements come from the discussion (options evaluated, judgments about motor and sensory status); considered operations are recorded as possible procedures, not as performed.
